L15 normal-to-port velocity alone does not establish pointwise zero viscous power: normal viscous stress can survive, as the local alignment counterexample shows. Fully developed pipe flow is an explicit sufficient zero-work case. This is not a claim that normal velocity everywhere on a smooth planar incompressible port permits nonzero Newtonian normal traction: tangential derivatives and continuity impose an additional zero-normal-strain condition in that special case.
L15/L16 stress notation and energy symbols translated explicitly: board tau(total),u(internal),e(total) become T,e,epsilon; h reserved for enthalpy and falling distance renamed d.
L16 loss and periodic remarks qualified: first law alone does not establish universal nonnegative loss; exact cycle-mean storage vanishes at any period, while flux means retain correlations.
L16 apparent reservoir-to-tube pressure jump interpreted as collapsed entrance acceleration region, not physical pressure discontinuity.

L17 board/spoken V18.77 and suction264.2Pa differ from recalculation using stipulated500W,1.5kg/m3,0.1m2:18.820721m/s,265.664642Pa. Board0.2mmHg conversion omitted as incorrect; no mercury property conversion relied upon.

L17 head sketch correctly jumps across fan; nearby broad spoken constant-head statement is qualified to passive lossless portions. Vehicle power-cubic analogy distinguished from energy per distance and actual fuel use.

No empirical loss coefficient, diffuser angle, generic fan/motor efficiency, real water property or vapour-pressure value claimed. All added round material/loss/efficiency inputs are explicitly teaching assumptions.
